The short morning stiffness, bony nodes without synovitis, and central erosions with osteophytes and “gull-wing” changes strongly support OA; psoriasis alone does not establish PsA.  
**I would not switch to or add a biologic “to cover the joints”**: there is no demonstrated active PsA, and biologics are not recommended for erosive hand OA.  
Treat with education, hand exercises/occupational therapy, thumb-base orthoses and topical NSAIDs, considering a short course of oral NSAIDs only after assessing renal, gastrointestinal and cardiovascular risks and medication interactions.  
Methotrexate continuation or adjustment should be guided by her skin disease, treatment burden and safety monitoring—not by these OA changes.  
Normal CRP and methotrexate treatment do not absolutely exclude coexisting PsA, so reassess if soft-tissue swelling, prolonged morning stiffness, dactylitis or enthesitis emerges, reserving targeted ultrasound for genuine uncertainty about inflammatory synovitis.
